clue.text: Feature of Texas suggesting offer of carrot agreeable?

definitions.meaning: the oil pump whose beam rocks up and down is a familiar sight on Texan oilfields
a beast of burden bobbing its head in assent to a proffered carrot

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what a Texas landmark might be telling someone holding out a carrot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half literally: a donkey that nods is agreeing to the carrot it has been offered.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname comes from the pump's beam rising and falling like the head of a bowing beast of burden.

clue.text: Tell to insert into that which rises

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill
to fit something is to insert it in place

explanation.surface: An instruction to tell someone to put something into a thing that goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to insert' is a verb phrase standing for its synonym; 'into' nests it, and 'which rises' reads the result upwards in this down entry, giving YFITON backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone formally is to tell them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: See 1 across
Ship opening line

definitions.meaning: a vessel built to cut a channel through frozen seas
a remark made to ease awkwardness when strangers first meet

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the image of breaking through a frozen surface, literally at sea or socially.

clue.text: Plant has top of spine covered in blood

indicators.note: covered in says the first letter is wrapped inside the blood word

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: top of a down-clue word takes its first letter

explanation.surface: A plant whose spines carry a spot of blood at their tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes S from spine, and 'covered in' puts it inside GORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, also called furze, is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Bovine given double sex change becomes Bombay duck

indicators.note: two letters change from female to male, so each F becomes an M

parts.note: a buffalo is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A cow undergoes a transformation twice over and turns into a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: F is female and M male, so swapping both Fs of BUFFALO for Ms gives the answer. 'Bombay duck' is not a bird but a dried fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The bummalo is a small South Asian fish which, salted and dried, is sold as Bombay duck.

clue.text: Awful lot of money on game

parts.note: awful means bad
a mint is a large sum of money, as in 'cost a mint'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a game costs a dreadful amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Staff given spice

definitions.meaning: a ceremonial rod carried as a symbol of authority
the dried outer covering of the nutmeg used to flavour food

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an official's ceremonial club and a spice taken from nutmeg.

clue.text: Film-maker showing a corrupt dictator up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: rot is corruption or decay
Idi Amin was the brutal dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A film-maker exposes a crooked tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns both the corrupt word and the tyrant together, giving NIMATOR; no single piece reversed would do.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator makes cartoon films, drawing or modelling the frames, so is a kind of film-maker.

clue.text: Mention new treatment initially as 12

indicators.note: new says the letters of mention are made into something fresh
initially takes the first letter of the word after

explanation.surface: Instructions to bring up a new treatment as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MENTION into OINTMEN, and 'initially' adds T from treatment. 12 refers to the answer at 12 across, a soothing salve.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a soothing preparation rubbed on the skin, which is what the 12 answer describes.

clue.text: For example, perfect figures deteriorate finally

parts.note: tens are numbers, figures

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Even perfect numbers decline in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The perfect in grammar (I have done) is a verb form, so it is an example of the answer, not praise.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the perfect is one of the verb forms showing time, hence an instance of this category.

clue.text: Introduce fresh drop

indicators.note: fresh says the letters of introduce are made anew

explanation.surface: Bringing in something new causes a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduce fresh' looks like a verb phrase about novelty; 'fresh' rearranges INTRODUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop in price or level is a lessening, a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Iris requires fine adjustment of slide rule

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads

indicators.note: adjustment of says the letters of slide rule are reset into a new order

explanation.surface: A flower needs a delicate tweak to a calculating instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment of' rearranges SLIDE RULE into LEURDELIS after F.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic lily of France is based on the iris flower, so the iris can be called by this name.

clue.text: Bush spoke of a nuclear weapon, perhaps, which is soothing

indicators.note: George W Bush's way of saying words is mimicked, so what follows is heard rather than read

parts.note: a nuclear weapon is one kind of bomb

explanation.surface: A president talks about atomic arms, which is somehow calming.
explanation.walkthrough: In an American accent the word for an explosive device rhymes with calm; the clue nods to Bush's famous 'nucular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm is something soothing; the noun is used here for that which soothes.

clue.text: Uncompromising engineers describing a 325-day year?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
take away the forty days of Lent from 365 and you get a year with no Lent

explanation.surface: Stubborn engineers working out a calendar of 325 days.
explanation.walkthrough: Lent lasts forty days, so a year of 325 days is one without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless means unyielding and unremitting, which is what uncompromising also means.

clue.text: Ordinal in West to show bottom face up?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: Mae West, the American film star
ninth is an ordinal number
to moon is to bare one's backside

explanation.surface: A coarse instruction to bare one's backside in a western setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' nests the number in the film star's name; Mae West, not a compass point. The face of the man in the moon is up in the sky, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the face people imagine on the full moon, looking down from high above.

clue.text: Old promise is claimed by Heather to be adoring

parts.note: the vow made at a wedding, a long-standing form of promise

indicators.note: claimed by says the next word swallows the letters of is

parts.note: ling is a common heather
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old vow is taken over by a woman named Heather, who worships it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is claimed by' nests the two letters; Heather looks like a woman's name but is the moorland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolising someone means worshipping and adoring them excessively; the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Are homeless snails so slow?

parts.note: snails without shells are slugs, and a word for slow describes being rather like them

explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish means slow-moving and lethargic, like the shell-less molluscs it is named after.

clue.text: The cause of a martyr is wonderful!

definitions.meaning: something one would give one's life for
informal praise for something irresistibly good

explanation.definitionFit: A martyr's cause is literally worth dying for, while the idiom calls something superb in the same words.

clue.text: Supple ladies and gentlemen accompany first of triathletes into ebbing river

parts.note: Ladies and Gents are public toilets, loos

indicators.note: into says the joined pieces go inside the river
an ebbing river flows back, so its name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to join someone is to accompany them

indicators.note: first of takes the first letter of the word after

explanation.surface: Flexible athletes, men and women, enter a receding river in a triathlon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' turns the river to EED; 'into' puts the joining word plus T (from 'first of triathletes') inside, giving EJOINTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-jointed describes limbs that move freely, so it is a synonym for supple.

clue.text: End of a canal destroyed 'em, they say

indicators.note: they say means the words are heard, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: wrecked them, run together in casual speech

explanation.surface: A canal's end ruined them, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, the gut, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The final section of the large intestine is the last part of the alimentary canal.

clue.text: Board promoting setter, as setter might say?

indicators.note: promoting raises the word, which in a down entry reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: the setter of the puzzle refers to himself as me
a setter is a gun dog, and a dog says bark

explanation.surface: A setter boosting himself, as he might put it, to board.
explanation.walkthrough: The first setter is the crossword compiler, the second the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark on a ship or plane is to board it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Network where mournful tune endlessly given backing

indicators.note: backing turns the letters to run backwards
endlessly removes the final letter

parts.note: a dirge is a lament

explanation.surface: A network where a sad song is played on repeat and supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts DIRGE to DIRG, and 'given backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines, as in the electricity grid.

clue.text: Small-timer replaced small flower

indicators.note: replaced says the letters of small-timer are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A petty crook is swapped for a modest bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower is something that flows, here a little stream, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill stream is a small watercourse driving a mill wheel, and a flower in crosswords is something that flows.

clue.text: Thin line, American, heading to the bottom

indicators.note: the first letter of the word drops to the foot of this down entry

parts.note: Yank is slang for an American

explanation.surface: A thin American queues up, then heads downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to the bottom' moves the Y of YANK to its end, giving ANKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanky means tall and thin, so it is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Among Indians, a rich, traditional garment

indicators.note: among says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Among Indians, a wealthy and customary form of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the traditional draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Even having pierced the back of the head, there's swelling

indicators.note: piercing says one piece goes through the middle of the other

parts.note: the inion is the bump on the skull at the back of the head
flat means even, level

explanation.surface: A level object has stabbed the back of someone's skull, causing a bump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having pierced' nests one piece in the other; the inion is an anatomical term solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is the act of swelling up, as of a balloon or prices.

clue.text: Old painting reflected more

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: reflected shows the word as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: An old picture seen in a mirror shows something more.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more of something.

clue.text: Fish off course passing close to beach

indicators.note: close to takes the last letter of the word after

parts.note: erring means going astray

explanation.surface: A fish swims astray past the end of a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives H, the last letter of beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a common silvery food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Bovine masks like royal veil

indicators.note: masks says one piece covers and holds the other

parts.note: the yak is a bovine of Tibet
as means like
HM is His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A cow covers its face like a royal veil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masks' nests the two short pieces inside the Tibetan ox, with 'royal' as the usual abbreviation for the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is the veil worn by some Muslim women to cover the face in public.
